title: When the Team Is Off Track
body: Find the real problem and rebuild one routine over 30 days.
notes: Use a real group or one of two fictional cases.
aria: When the Team Is Off Track. Find the real problem and rebuild one routine over 30 days.

title: Culture Overhaul
body: Part V includes the confirmed Chapter 23 theme of culture spreading through people.
notes: Recommend L1–L4 first.
aria: Culture Overhaul. Part V includes the confirmed Chapter 23 theme of culture spreading through people.

title: When nobody is watching
body: Culture shows up in repeated behavior when the official lead is absent.
notes: Use an unattended sign-in table.
aria: When nobody is watching. Culture shows up in repeated behavior when the official lead is absent.

title: Three decisions
body: Find the real problem, identify who leads in your absence and run the change.
notes: Outline one month of repetition. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Three decisions. Find the real problem, identify who leads in your absence and run the change.

title: Activity: describe the slip
body: Record one observable change without naming peers.
notes: Separate a late start from a guess about effort.
aria: Activity: describe the slip. Record one observable change without naming peers.

title: Look at your system first
body: Check how your own instructions, routines and follow-up contribute.
notes: Ask what someone new is told. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Look at your system first. Check how your own instructions, routines and follow-up contribute.

title: A diagnostic question
body: Test for an unclear standard, missing follow-up, a skills gap, a schedule problem or a leader ignoring a standard.
notes: Seek evidence before choosing.
aria: A diagnostic question. Test for an unclear standard, missing follow-up, a skills gap, a schedule problem or a leader ignoring a standard.

title: Case A: the late club
body: A fictional club starts 15 minutes late and laughs it off.
notes: Check who has the key and when the agenda appears.
aria: Case A: the late club. A fictional club starts 15 minutes late and laughs it off.

title: Case B: the busy close
body: In a hypothetical restaurant, the closing station is messy after busy shifts.
notes: Inspect the handoff and available time.
aria: Case B: the busy close. In a hypothetical restaurant, the closing station is messy after busy shifts.

title: Activity: name the system problem
body: Describe the gap in one sentence someone could test.
notes: Use roles rather than names.
aria: Activity: name the system problem. Describe the gap in one sentence someone could test.

title: Mid-quiz: three decisions
body: Check the first place to look, behavior without supervision and a system-first explanation.
notes: Avoid diagnosing the group.
aria: Mid-quiz: three decisions. Check the first place to look, behavior without supervision and a system-first explanation.

title: Find out respectfully
body: Ask about a handoff, observe it with permission or review the outcome.
notes: No spying or secret recordings. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Find out respectfully. Ask about a handoff, observe it with permission or review the outcome.

title: Culture Carriers
body: Chapter 23 describes a person who lives the standard so others can learn it.
notes: Use behavior as the evidence. [BRENEN EXCERPT: 2–4 sentences from the mapped chapter, approved by Brenen]
aria: Culture Carriers. Chapter 23 describes a person who lives the standard so others can learn it.

title: Who models the routine?
body: Look for someone who consistently closes the loop when nobody prompts them.
notes: Distinguish this from popularity.
aria: Who models the routine?. Look for someone who consistently closes the loop when nobody prompts them.

title: Invite a Culture Carrier
body: Ask them to model one opening, closing or pairing task.
notes: Keep the work bounded and voluntary. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Invite a Culture Carrier. Ask them to model one opening, closing or pairing task.

title: When the lead is part of the problem
body: Use a private factual conversation or involve the actual advisor or manager.
notes: Stay within your authority. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: When the lead is part of the problem. Use a private factual conversation or involve the actual advisor or manager.

title: Activity: identify roles
body: Describe who models the standard and who has the authority to follow up.
notes: No full names in stored notes.
aria: Activity: identify roles. Describe who models the standard and who has the authority to follow up.

title: One visible reset
body: Write one standard, choose a huddle or review, and schedule follow-up.
notes: Make the routine visible to a newcomer. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: One visible reset. Write one standard, choose a huddle or review, and schedule follow-up.

title: Repeat the repair
body: A one-off reward cannot make a late agenda appear on time.
notes: Build a cue for repetition. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Repeat the repair. A one-off reward cannot make a late agenda appear on time.

title: A four-week calendar
body: Reset in week one, repeat in weeks two and three, and review in week four.
notes: Name a person and time for each step.
aria: A four-week calendar. Reset in week one, repeat in weeks two and three, and review in week four.

title: Activity: fill the 30-day plan
body: Apply each week to the club or closing example.
notes: Add an observable measure.
aria: Activity: fill the 30-day plan. Apply each week to the club or closing example.

title: Screen recording: a culture slip
body: Plan a 10–12 minute walkthrough of a restaurant case and paper plan.
notes: Use a clearly fictional narrated case pending Brenen's approved story. [BRENEN MAP] Official theme from the published site/templates, but no chapter number/title is confirmed. Brenen will map this lesson to the actual chapter before the paid version ships. Do not invent a title.
aria: Screen recording: a culture slip. Plan a 10–12 minute walkthrough of a restaurant case and paper plan.

title: Shortcuts to avoid
body: Changing a slogan, shaming a group or adding twelve rules can hide the actual problem.
notes: Compare with one testable routine.
aria: Shortcuts to avoid. Changing a slogan, shaming a group or adding twelve rules can hide the actual problem.

title: When to get help
body: For harassment, discrimination, violence or safety issues, go to a trusted adult, manager or school process.
notes: A student does not have to investigate or resolve harm alone.
aria: When to get help. For harassment, discrimination, violence or safety issues, go to a trusted adult, manager or school process.

title: A resume result you can support
body: Describe what happened across real meetings only if observed.
notes: Worked example must identify the actual dates or count.
aria: A resume result you can support. Describe what happened across real meetings only if observed.

title: Worksheet: 30-Day Overhaul Plan
body: Record the system problem, Culture Carrier role, weekly plan and escalation contact role.
notes: Use a role without personal contact details.
aria: Worksheet: 30-Day Overhaul Plan. Record the system problem, Culture Carrier role, weekly plan and escalation contact role.

title: Common traps
body: Avoid generational blame, playing hero or giving up after one week.
notes: Ask which part of your routine is missing.
aria: Common traps. Avoid generational blame, playing hero or giving up after one week.

title: What will last?
body: Connect the system check, Chapter 23 and repetition.
notes: Show the link in one case.
aria: What will last?. Connect the system check, Chapter 23 and repetition.

title: The two tracks
body: Students can continue into the AI classes after leadership.
notes: Do not assume everyone completed prior classes.
aria: The two tracks. Students can continue into the AI classes after leadership.

title: Optional completion line
body: Preview a record describing this class.
notes: It carries no school or licensing credit.
aria: Optional completion line. Preview a record describing this class.

title: End question: where to start
body: Choose the first evidence to examine in a drifting team.
notes: Return to the leader's routine.
aria: End question: where to start. Choose the first evidence to examine in a drifting team.

title: End question: Culture Carrier
body: Identify a modeled behavior from Chapter 23.
notes: Separate popularity from evidence.
aria: End question: Culture Carrier. Identify a modeled behavior from Chapter 23.

title: End question: repetition
body: Compare a month of follow-up with a single pep talk.
notes: Choose the measurable plan.
aria: End question: repetition. Compare a month of follow-up with a single pep talk.

title: End question: adult involvement
body: Identify a scenario needing a trusted adult or formal process.
notes: Never make a student handle danger alone.
aria: End question: adult involvement. Identify a scenario needing a trusted adult or formal process.

title: End question: a truthful result
body: Choose a bullet supported by the observed meeting record.
notes: Remove claims without evidence.
aria: End question: a truthful result. Choose a bullet supported by the observed meeting record.

title: Answer review
body: Explain the five decisions and allow a retry.
notes: Four correct completes the class.
aria: Answer review. Explain the five decisions and allow a retry.

title: Track recap: ownership
body: Link one small repair to a standard you held.
notes: Only claim practiced behavior.
aria: Track recap: ownership. Link one small repair to a standard you held.

title: Track recap: people and stage
body: Identify an actual training conversation or environment change.
notes: Make it specific enough to describe aloud.
aria: Track recap: people and stage. Identify an actual training conversation or environment change.

title: Track recap: techniques
body: Choose a huddle or follow-up skill only if you used it.
notes: Offer a modest resume wording.
aria: Track recap: techniques. Choose a huddle or follow-up skill only if you used it.

title: Close the month
body: Set the date for the fourth-week review.
notes: Keep the plan and record what actually happened.
aria: Close the month. Set the date for the fourth-week review.
